## See what 5 builders are making with Gemini 4 Carbon

These ambitious real-world projects simulate live physics, untangle messy data, turn a single reference image into a 3D design, and more.

We are seeing developers use Gemini 4 Carbon to build complex simulations, interactive data tools, and detailed virtual environments. This model helps you reason deeply and perform extended verification tasks for your most demanding projects. You can start building with Carbon today through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Android Studio, or your preferred business integration.

• We are highlighting five creative projects that demonstrate the deep reasoning capabilities of Gemini 4 Carbon.

• You can use this model to simulate complex physical environments, large particle systems, and interactive tools.

• Developers are currently using Carbon to build everything from detailed virtual laboratories to intricate glass games.

• You can access Carbon through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Android Studio, and other platforms.

We recently launched Gemini 4 Carbon, our most capable model for complex technical projects. People are already using it to simulate millions of moving particles, build interactive 3D environments, and turn messy public data into useful tools. It handles deep reasoning and detailed verification, making it easier for you to create sophisticated software or realistic simulations. You can start building with Carbon today through our developer tools and business platforms.

## Explore other styles:

Gemini 4 Carbon was built for tasks that push the limits of a model’s intelligence, and builders are putting it to the test.

Since we rolled out Carbon more broadly last week, we've seen the community lean into the model’s ability to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops. Find five impressive projects that demonstrate Carbon's capabilities below.

## Render a wind-swept meadow.

Glitter Gal (@GlitterPixely on X) coded a meadow of 52,000 wildflowers and grass blades from scratch in CUDA and C++ with Carbon, synthesizing the wind to match every gust.

## Create a simulation with a million moving parts.

Chubby (@kimmonismuson X) wanted to see over a million glowing particles swirl and shift like live tidal currents, using Carbon to simulate 1,048,576 particles in real time with WebGPU.

## Make a glass game that shatters.

Andrew V (@AI_Andrew on X) wondered what a block-stacking game would feel like if every piece were made of fragile stained glass; Carbon simulated how the tower catches the light, rings when tapped, and shatters into shards when it falls.

## Turn disorganized data into interactive tools.

Giyu_codes (@giyu_codes on X) went looking for underserved industries buried in messy public records, pairing with Carbon to turn scattered public datasets into 14 interactive tools with live 3D visuals. Explore all 14 builds in their thread .

## Build a mesmerizing laboratory.

Starting from a single reference image, The Bugged Dev (@thebuggeddev on X) brought a 19th-century Parisian optics lab to life with Carbon, complete with 92 brass and glass instruments you can actually test and tune.

Developers can build with Carbon with the Gemini API paid tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio . Google AI Ultra subscribers can try it in Google Antigravity , AI Studio, the Gemini app , and AI Mode in Search . And Gemini for business users can access it via the API or model drop down, Google Antigravity, or CodeMender.

• مشروع آخر يحاكي 1,048,576 جسيماً متوهجاً في الزمن الحقيقي باستخدام WebGPU.

• مشروع ثالث لعبة تكديس كتل زجاجية تتحطم.

• يتوفر النموذج عبر Gemini API وGoogle AI Studio وAndroid Studio ومنصات أخرى.

تُظهر هذه الأمثلة قدرة النموذج على التفكير العميق وحلقات التحقق الممتدة في المهام الصعبة.
